subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw keep this broad RFC as the canonical multi-agent collaboration direction and split it into scoped core/plugin tracks, or reject/re-scope the broad stack toward plugin/ClawHub-only work?
rationale: The remaining work chooses product architecture, config/state ownership, security boundaries, and whether heavy orchestration belongs in core or plugin APIs; those choices cannot be safely inferred from source inspection alone.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design umbrella, use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42475 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65403 for narrower slices, and create/route additional scoped design items only after owner review.

options.title: Core stack direction
options.body: Sponsor a native core design with SQLite state, migrations, config schema, budget admission, blackboard tools, memory visibility, and explicit security policy before implementation PRs.

options.title: Plugin/API-first direction
options.body: Decline a broad core stack for now and focus on plugin SDK or ClawHub extension seams that let external packages provide orchestration without expanding core defaults.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design umbrella, use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42475 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65403 for narrower slices, and create/route additional scoped design items only after owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from current subagent/config history, VISION/product-boundary history, and related RFC scope review.
